claims.statement: AST code search consumes one native scan --json=stream object per match, with upstream structural selection owned by ast-grep and semantic selection owned by jev-grep.

Code candidates evaluate only text rather than lines context and remain independent even when adjacent, nested, overlapping or duplicated; the AST branch bypasses adjacent grouping and join-threshold.
Each validated uncapped AST candidate receives one sequential logical match evaluation with its text as API state; retries can produce multiple transport attempts.
Selected code results and first source listings are flushed immediately without transport EOF, while ast-grep source stdin itself is read to EOF before candidate production.
AST validation requires non-NUL string text, nonempty string file, ordered nonnegative integer byte and line/column coordinates consistent with UTF-8 text, and string language when present.

AST line consistency uses LF counts, columns use Unicode character counts, and output converts lines to one-based inclusive spans excluding an empty trailing-LF line while preserving half-open upstream bytes.
Malformed AST shapes including arrays, inconsistent coordinates, invalid UTF-8, NUL and oversized candidates fail before inference with transport name and physical JSONL line diagnostics.

AST validation checks supplied text/range consistency but never reopens upstream source files or checks source changes, allowing saved candidate streams to be queried independently of the source tree.

Physical JSONL line and decoded candidate text limits are separate, both default to 16384 bytes, and an oversized AST node fails rather than splitting; serialized repeated context may require a larger line limit without increasing model context.
One invocation-wide CodeSourceAccounting tracks selected counts and listing flags by exact upstream file string across interleaved candidates and multiple JSONL inputs, without path canonicalization.

Code-mode max-count limits selected candidates per upstream source, suppressing later inference for capped sources while continuing physical, schema, coordinate and text-size validation and processing other sources.
Code count mode emits totals at successful invocation completion in first-seen source order including zero selections, omits sources with no candidates, and emits nothing for an empty stream.
Code files-with-matches prints each upstream source once without stopping further evaluation, whereas quiet mode stops the invocation at the first selected candidate.

Code selection uses probability at or above threshold unless inverted, counts duplicate selected candidates separately, and emits JSON code fragments with source text basis, preserved text and optional language and false split flags; human output always includes source and byte/line ranges and adds a missing final newline.
Only exact upstream STDIN maps to JSON stdin with null path and human (stdin); count/list retain STDIN, and transport stdin versus file does not determine code source identity.
CLI globs, hidden and no-ignore options select JSONL transport inputs, not candidate source paths; source selection and language-specific node boundaries must be configured upstream in ast-grep.

The documented changed-file Git pipeline scans current working versions of all functions in tracked changed existing Rust files against HEAD, excludes untracked and deleted behavior, preserves paths with NUL delimiters and arrays, avoids default-directory scanning on an empty list, and checks Git separately to avoid hidden process-substitution failure.

EOF cannot communicate upstream exit status to jev-grep, so pipefail is needed; consumer statuses are 0 for selection, 1 for none and 2 for errors, earlier output is not retracted on failure, quiet stopping may cause upstream SIGPIPE, and downstream broken pipes exit cleanly.

Focused CLI regression tests verify exact native AST text and coordinates, ignored context, stdin identity and pre-EOF output, pre-inference validation, interleaved and multiple-transport accounting, ordered counts and once-per-source listings using an HTTP stub rather than establishing semantic quality.
